\subsection{Forward-Pass Interventions}
\label{sec:forward_results}

The SGS results establish gradient stopping as categorically insufficient. We test two forward-pass alternatives (Table~\ref{tab:intervention_hierarchy}). \textbf{RAVE} (value-level capping) fails at both ceiling values: the EMA anchor tracks biased imagined values during CIVO onset, rendering the ceiling ineffective. \textbf{TCN} (representation-level noise) exhibits dose-dependent behavior: $\sigma{=}0.5$ produces oscillatory CIVO in both seeds (peak NVE $4.0\times$ and $1.6\times$; eval $\leq 40\%$ of baseline), while $\sigma{=}0.2$ maintains NVE below $1.0\times$ throughout training (peak $0.91\times$ at 95K) with eval reaching $90\%$ of baseline (821.1 at 175K). The $\sigma{=}0.2$ result is the first configuration in our study to fully prevent CIVO while preserving competitive performance ($n{=}1$ seed, Walker Walk; additional seeds pending). On Cheetah Run, $\sigma{=}0.2$ is insufficient (NVE $= 1.9\times$ at 55K), consistent with Cheetah's higher CIVO severity ($8$--$108\times$ vs.\ Walker's $2$--$6\times$).

The three-level intervention hierarchy (Table~\ref{tab:intervention_hierarchy}) reveals a monotonic relationship between intervention depth and efficacy: gradient-level (0--17\%), output-level (0\%), representation-level (0--100\%), with only calibrated representation-level noise succeeding. This ordering is consistent with CIVO's locus in the temporal embedding's forward-pass contribution to latent representations.
